newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - BSkyB says box price to boost digital tv.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - BSkyB says box price to boost digital tv.

text.p: British Sky Broadcasting Plc said on Friday plans to sell set-top boxes for under 200 stg should encourage subscriptions to the UK digital satellite services it plans to launch in spring 1998.

"Coming in at 200 stg will have a significant impact on relative take-up," BSkyB deputy managing director David Chance said in a telephone interview when asked about the slow start for digital services launched by broadcasters in other parts of Europe.
Chance said BSkyB had been able to get the key components of its digital launch in place by going a little later than other operators.

These include the establishment of the British Interactive Broadcasting (BIB) venture which will provide interactive services such as home shopping and subsidise the cost of the set-top boxes. BSkyB's partners in BIB are British Telecommunications Plc, Midland Bank Plc and Matsushita.
Chance said BSkyB had also been able to reap "fairly significant" cost benefits by securing capacity on the new Astra 2A satellite to be launched in December.

Chance said BSkyB had been talking to a number of cable companies about securing carriage for its new 200-channel digital TV service. The plan is to make it available either "direct to home" via a dish or alternatively via cable, as is the case for existing analogue services.
BSkyB is negotiating with Hollywood studios to secure pay-per-view rights for films and Chance said deals would be sought on a revenue-sharing basis.
He would not be drawn on the possible launch of pay-per-view coverage of English premier league soccer but did say that similar revenue sharing deals could be struck with the clubs.

Chance and chief executive Sam Chisholm are both giving up their full-time positions at BSkyB at the end of the year although both will remain as consultants and members of the board. Mark Booth, chief operating officer of JSkyB, will take over as chief executive in January.
Chance said his consultancy arrangement meant he would be working full-time for BSkyB until the middle of next year as the company moved into the digital era.
"I've put a lot of the last 10 years of my life into this company and I'm determined to help it in this critical phase," he said.
